items.title: Standalone and Home Assistant add-on backend
items.text:
This reference covers the current Python backend, configured with panels.yaml. For new installations, start with the main Home Assistant add-on guide and web editor guide.

These pages remain available at their existing standalone URLs. They describe the same backend as the main documentation, not AppDaemon.

  • Getting started
  • Configuration
  • Import from AppDaemon
  • Cards, screensaver, and entities
  • Connection modes and troubleshooting

items.title: Supported card types
items.text:
• cardEntities
  • cardGrid
  • cardQR
  • cardPower
  • cardMedia
  • cardThermo
  • cardAlarm
  • cardUnlock

items.title: Common card keys
items.text: key required type description type yes string Card type. title no string Card title. key no string Navigation key used by navigate.<key>.

items.title: cardEntities and cardGrid
items.text:
- type: cardEntities
  title: Main
  key: main
  entities:
    - entity: light.kitchen
    - entity: navigate.settings
      icon: mdi:cog
  • entities is required.
  • cardGrid auto-switches to cardGrid2 if more than 6 entities are present.

items.title: cardQR
items.text:
- type: cardQR
  title: Guest WiFi
  qrCode: "WIFI:S:myssid;T:WPA;P:mypassword;;"
  entities:
    - entity: iText.myssid
      name: SSID
      icon: mdi:wifi

Keys:

  • qrCode optional (default value exists, but set it explicitly)
  • supports optional entity / entities

items.title: cardPower
items.text:
- type: cardPower
  title: Energy
  entities:
    - entity: sensor.house_power
    - entity: delete
    - entity: sensor.solar_power

Notes:

  • entities is required.
  • Set speed on each entity to control animation. It accepts numbers or Home Assistant templates, with or without the ha: prefix.
  • Speeds are clamped to the TFT range of -120 to 120. Negative values reverse the flow; zero stops it. Invalid or unavailable values use zero. Fractional values are truncated toward zero.
- type: cardPower
  title: Energy
  entities:
    - entity: sensor.house_power
    - entity: delete
    - entity: sensor.solar_power
      speed: '{{ states("sensor.solar_animation_speed") }}'

items.title: cardMedia
items.text:
- type: cardMedia
  title: Living Room
  entity: media_player.living_room
  entities:
    - entity: light.ambient
    - entity: switch.tv_bias_light

Notes:

  • Set entity to the main media entity; the editor requires it for media, thermostat, and alarm cards.
  • Additional entities are rendered as action buttons on the bottom row.

items.title: cardThermo
items.text:
- type: cardThermo
  title: Heating
  entity: climate.downstairs
  supported_modes: ["heat", "off"]

Keys:

  • entity required
  • supported_modes optional (filters shown HVAC mode buttons)

items.title: cardAlarm
items.text:
- type: cardAlarm
  title: House Alarm
  entity: alarm_control_panel.house
  supported_modes: ["arm_home", "arm_away", "arm_night"]

Keys:

  • entity required
  • supported_modes optional

items.title: cardUnlock
items.text:
- type: cardUnlock
  title: Admin
  pin: 1234
  destination: navigate.admin

Keys:

  • pin required
  • destination required

Typical target in hiddenCards:

hiddenCards:
  - type: cardGrid
    key: admin
    title: Admin
    entities:
      - entity: switch.maintenance_mode

items.title: Hidden-card navigation (4.8.5+)
items.text:
Hidden cards retain their left-hand Back/Up button. Configure navItem2 to add a right-hand button, for example a shortcut to a card with key: home:

hiddenCards:
  - type: cardGrid
    title: Lights
    key: lights
    navItem2:
      entity: navigate.home
      icon: mdi:home
    entities:
      - entity: light.kitchen

Main cards continue to use automatic previous/next navigation.

items.title: Configuration: panels.yaml
items.text:
The runtime reads one YAML file (default: ./panels.yaml, add-on mode: /config/panels.yaml).

Use the web editor to manage this file. For a complete starting configuration, see your first panel. Snippets in the card and screensaver references belong under nspanels.<panel_name>. Do not wrap them in AppDaemon module, class, or config keys.

items.title: Top-level keys
items.text: key required type default description nspanels yes object none Map of panel definitions. home_assistant_address recommended string none Home Assistant base URL. In add-on mode it is auto-filled as http://supervisor if missing. home_assistant_token recommended string none Long-lived token or Supervisor token. mqtt_server required in MQTT mode string from env MQTT host. mqtt_port required in MQTT mode int from env MQTT port. mqtt_username required in MQTT mode string from env MQTT username. mqtt_password required in MQTT mode string from env MQTT password. use_ha_api optional boolean false When true, MQTT input mode is disabled and HA event mode is used. timeZone optional string Europe/Berlin Global fallback for panel timeZone. hiddenCards optional list [] Global fallback for panel hiddenCards.

items.title: Panel keys (nspanels.<name>)
items.text: key required type default description panelRecvTopic yes string none Receive channel for panel events. panelSendTopic yes string none Send channel for panel commands. locale yes string none Locale used for translations and date formatting. timeZone recommended string from top-level timeZone Time zone for clock. timeFormat yes string none Python strftime format. dateFormat yes string none Babel date format (example: full, medium). model optional string eu Panel model (eu, us-p, us-l). temp_unit optional string celsius Thermostat card unit (celsius or fahrenheit). sleepTimeout optional int 20 Seconds before screensaver. sleepBrightness optional int, entity_id, or schedule 10 Screensaver brightness. screenBrightness optional int, entity_id, or schedule 100 Active-screen brightness. sleepTracking optional entity_id none Forces sleep brightness to 0 when entity state matches sleepTrackingZones. sleepTrackingZones optional list ["not_home", "off"] States that trigger forced dimming. sleepOverride optional object none Override sleep brightness when entity is on/true/home. defaultBackgroundColor optional string ha-dark ha-dark or black. featExperimentalSliders optional int 0 Forwarded in dimmode command. defaultCard optional string none Default card when leaving screensaver (navigate.<key>). screensaver yes object none Screensaver definition. cards yes list none At least one supported top-level card is required when saving in the editor. hiddenCards optional list [] Hidden cards addressable through navigate.<key>.

items.title: Brightness behavior
items.text:
• Integer values are used directly.
  • Entity values read Home Assistant state and cast to number.
  • Daily time/value schedules are supported for both sleep and active-screen brightness.

Example:

sleepBrightness: input_number.nspanel_sleep
screenBrightness: input_number.nspanel_awake
sleepTracking: person.john
sleepTrackingZones: ["not_home", "off"]
sleepOverride:
  entity: light.bedroom
  brightness: 30

items.title: Web editor (Home Assistant add-on)
items.text: From add-on version 4.8.0, Open Web UI provides a visual panel/card/entity editor and a full YAML editor. Import existing add-on or AppDaemon YAML into a draft, review warnings, and save to apply. Saves create panels.yaml.bak and reload the backend; stale browser drafts cannot overwrite newer disk revisions. Home Assistant ingress is the default access mode. Standalone Docker installations can opt into direct access with WEB_STANDALONE=true and WEB_PASSWORD; see the standalone guide.

items.title: TFT firmware updates (4.8.1+)
items.text:
At panel startup, the backend checks the reported TFT version and model against its pinned firmware target (currently protocol version 53, release v4.7.3, matching the former AppDaemon target). It does not query the latest GitHub release. A backend release can advance this target separately from its add-on version.

Set TFT firmware updates in the visual editor, or add the following under your panel:

updateMode: auto-notify
  • auto-notify (default): show an Install/Dismiss dialog on the physical panel when an update is needed.
  • auto: start an update automatically when the installed version is older. A model change still requires confirmation.
  • manual: do not offer or start TFT updates.

Dismissing a prompt suppresses further prompts until the backend restarts. A newer TFT on the same model is not downgraded. The backend sends at most one flash request per panel per backend run; check device logs before restarting to retry a failed transfer. Keep power connected while flashing. A new startup message reports the resulting version; no startup after ten minutes is logged as an unconfirmed update, not success.

Tasmota installations need the Berry driver with FlashNextion support and a panelSendTopic ending in /CustomSend. Compatible ESPHome installations use the existing nspanelui_api_call service with command 255; support depends on the installed ESPHome component. TFTs older than protocol version 16 require manual flashing. Berry driver updates remain manual.

Advanced YAML options retain the AppDaemon names displayURL-EU, displayURL-US-P, and displayURL-US-L. Only the URL for the selected model is used. Custom URLs must use HTTP and be reachable from the panel. Set displayFirmwareVersion to the protocol version embedded in a custom TFT (not its release string), for example:

updateMode: auto-notify
displayURL-EU: http://homeassistant.local:8123/local/nspanel.tft
displayFirmwareVersion: 53

items.title: Dynamic brightness
items.text:
Set the following under your panel in the YAML editor (or All panel options using JSON):

timeZone: Europe/Berlin
sleepBrightness:
  - time: "07:00"
    value: 35
  - time: "22:00"
    value: 0

This uses brightness 35 during the day and 0 overnight. Times are daily local wall-clock times in the panel's timeZone; quote them in YAML. HH:MM and HH:MM:SS are accepted. Entries may be unordered but must have unique times and integer values from 0 to 100. The last entry from the previous day applies before the first entry, including after a restart. The backend checks schedules every second and sends a brightness command only when the resolved settings change. The same schedule format is supported by screenBrightness. Sunrise/sunset expressions are not supported.

For illumination-driven control, set sleepBrightness: input_number.nspanel_sleep and use a Home Assistant automation to update that helper from your illuminance sensor. A numeric sensor entity can also be used directly if its state already represents a desired brightness percentage. Values are clamped to 0–100; raw lux is not automatically converted into a brightness curve. Entity changes update the panel without a restart.

sleepTracking still forces sleep brightness to zero when its configured state matches; an active sleepOverride takes precedence over that and the schedule. An override brightness of zero is supported.

items.title: Connection Modes
items.text: The backend supports two panel input/output modes.

items.title: 1) MQTT mode (default)
items.text:
Enabled when:

  • mqtt_server is configured
  • use_ha_api is absent or false

Behavior:

  • Subscribes to every panel panelRecvTopic
  • Expects JSON payload containing CustomRecv
  • Publishes commands to panelSendTopic

Example receive payload:

{"CustomRecv":"event,startup,54,eu"}

items.title: 2) Home Assistant API mode (use_ha_api)
items.text:
Enabled when use_ha_api: true is set at the top level of panels.yaml.

Behavior:

  • Subscribes to HA event esphome.nspanel.data
  • Routes events by device_id (must match configured panelRecvTopic)
  • Sends panel commands by calling Home Assistant service:
  • <panelSendTopic>_nspanelui_api_call

Service payload shape:

data: "...panel command..."
command: 2

items.title: Common to both modes
items.text:
• Home Assistant websocket connection is used for entity state cache and service calls.
  • UI actions (button presses, sliders, mode selects) are translated to Home Assistant service calls.

items.title: Entities
items.text: Entities are used in cards and screensaver lists.

items.title: Entity keys
items.text: key required type description entity yes string Home Assistant entity id, or internal entity (navigate.*, delete, iText.*). name no string Display name override; supports ha: templates. icon no string or map Icon override (mdi:*), optionally per state. color no [r,g,b], template string, or map Color override, optionally per state. value no string Value override. font no string Icon font variant (small, medium, medium-icon, large). status no string Extra status entity for navigate.* items. effectList no list Custom light effect list for detail popup. attribute no string Weather attribute to display. day no int Weather daily forecast index. hour no int Weather hourly forecast index. unit no string Value suffix.

items.title: Internal entities
items.text:
• navigate.<key>: Navigate to card with matching key.
  • navigate.UP: Navigate back.
  • delete: Placeholder/empty slot.
  • iText.<text>: Static text entry.

items.title: Template-based values
items.text:
The backend supports Home Assistant template rendering for selected fields when prefixed with ha::

  • icon: "ha:{{ ... }}"
  • color: "ha:{{ ... }}" (must evaluate to JSON RGB list)
  • value: "ha:{{ ... }}"
  • qrCode: "ha:{{ ... }}"

Example:

- entity: light.kitchen
  icon:
    "on": mdi:lightbulb
    "off": mdi:lightbulb-outline
  color:
    "on": [255, 210, 90]
    "off": [80, 120, 170]

items.title: Sensor display precision
items.text:
Numeric sensor values respect Home Assistant's resolved display precision, including the sensor's configured precision and integration-suggested precision when provided by HA. For example, 7.75165151099879 with precision 2 is sent as 7.75, and precision 0 produces 8. This applies before units and grid value icons are generated.

Precision changes in Home Assistant refresh the display without restarting the add-on. Sensors without precision metadata retain their original value; nonnumeric states such as unknown and unavailable are not rounded. Explicit value templates continue to take precedence. This does not change the underlying HA state or add locale-specific decimal separators. The US portrait entity-card character limit still applies.

items.title: Smaller sensor values on grids (4.8.3+)
items.text:
Set font on each entity to adjust its grid icon/value font. For numeric sensor readings, use medium or small:

- type: cardGrid
  title: Humidity
  entities:
    - entity: sensor.bedroom_humidity
      name: Bedroom
      font: medium
    - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
      name: Living room
      font: small

From 4.8.5, sensor readings in the grid icon/value area omit the unit, matching the former AppDaemon backend. For example, 8.44 g/m³ is displayed as 8.44, leaving more room for the reading and its font-selection suffix. To show the unit, include it in the entity name, such as Bedroom (g/m³). Entity cards and screensavers still show units.

The options are small, medium, medium-icon (an icon font), and large. Grid font selection also applies when cardGrid automatically switches to cardGrid2 for more than six entities. It affects the large icon/value area, not the entity label. It does not change sensor precision or the screensaver's separate status-icon font handling.

items.title: Dynamic templates (4.8.5+)
items.text:
Use ha: followed by a Home Assistant template for an entity's name, icon, color, or value:

- entity: sensor.bedroom_humidity
  name: 'ha:{{ states("sensor.bedroom_label") }}'
  color: 'ha:{{ states("sensor.bedroom_color") }}'

Name templates also work on navigate.* and iText.* items. The backend shares subscriptions for identical expressions and refreshes the displayed entity when the template result changes, including time-based templates. Subscriptions are restored after Home Assistant reconnects.

Color templates can return RGB text such as [223, 255, 0], (223, 255, 0), #dfff00, or rgb(223,255,0). RGB components must be integers from 0 to 255. Invalid or unavailable colors use the default entity color.

items.title: Weather forecast retrieval (4.8.5+)
items.text:
day: 0 selects the first daily forecast entry; day: 1 selects the next entry. hour: 0 likewise selects the first hourly entry. Dates depend on the forecast supplied by the Home Assistant integration.

Forecast entries share a cache by weather entity and forecast type. When rendered, missing or expired forecasts are refreshed in the background, with an eight-second response timeout and a five-minute cache lifetime. A successful refresh updates the panel automatically. Slow responses do not block panel interaction. Failed refreshes retain the last valid forecast and allow another attempt on a subsequent render after 30 seconds.

items.title: Getting started
items.text: For Home Assistant OS, install the add-on and use Open Web UI. The add-on discovers MQTT settings and uses the Supervisor HA connection. Leave HA address/token fields absent for this automatic connection.

items.title: Minimal panels.yaml
items.text:
Replace topics and entity IDs with your own. Save this in the editor or the add-on's /config/panels.yaml:

nspanels:
  kitchen:
    panelRecvTopic: tele/nspanel_kitchen/RESULT
    panelSendTopic: cmnd/nspanel_kitchen/CustomSend
    model: eu
    locale: en_US
    timeZone: Europe/Berlin
    timeFormat: "%H:%M"
    dateFormat: full
    screensaver:
      entities:
        - entity: weather.home
    cards:
      - type: cardEntities
        title: Kitchen
        key: home
        entities:
          - entity: light.kitchen

For Home Assistant Container or a standalone process, follow the standalone operation guide. Supply your own HA address/token and MQTT settings; enable authenticated standalone editor access as described in that guide.

items.title: Import YAML and migrate from AppDaemon
items.text: The web editor accepts the old add-on panels.yaml format and NSPanel entries from AppDaemon apps.yaml. An import creates a draft; it does not write to the running configuration until Save & apply.

items.title: Migration steps
items.text:
1. Export or copy your existing configuration before changing backends.
  2. Install the new add-on and open its web interface.
  3. Choose Import YAML, upload/paste the file, and select Preview import.
  4. Review the detected panels, skipped apps, migration warnings, and validation errors.
  5. Choose Add to draft to merge panel definitions while preserving current global connection settings. Duplicate names are rejected. Use Replace draft to replace the entire draft, including connection settings.
  6. Review the resulting YAML, replace example entities, and fix unsupported settings. Stop the old backend before applying the same MQTT topics.
  7. Select Save & apply and verify the add-on log and physical display.

The initial add-on configuration contains an example panel. Remove it if you merge an import and do not intend to use it. A successful save creates panels.yaml.bak containing the previous configuration; keep your own exported copy for longer-term rollback.

items.title: Recognized input
items.text:
Existing add-on YAML uses nspanels at the top level and retains its configuration fields. AppDaemon input must contain entries with module: nspanel-lovelace-ui or class: NsPanelLovelaceUIManager and a config mapping. Other AppDaemon apps are skipped with warnings.

# AppDaemon input
kitchen:
  module: nspanel-lovelace-ui
  class: NsPanelLovelaceUIManager
  config:
    panelRecvTopic: tele/nspanel_kitchen/RESULT
    panelSendTopic: cmnd/nspanel_kitchen/CustomSend
    cards:
      - type: cardEntities
        title: Kitchen
        entities:
          - entity: light.kitchen

The importer moves each config into nspanels.<name> and supplies missing locale: en_US, timeZone: Europe/Berlin, timeFormat: "%H:%M", dateFormat: full, and an empty screensaver. Review those defaults for your location. A missing card list must be populated before saving.

items.title: Converted settings
items.text: AppDaemon setting New backend Review timezone timeZone Time zone casing changes. dateFormatBabel dateFormat Babel format; a strftime-only format is replaced with full and warned about. featureExperimentalSliders featExperimentalSliders Boolean values become 0/1. screensaver.defaultCard Panel-level defaultCard Ensure the result is navigate.<key> for an existing card. Card temperatureUnit Panel-level temp_unit Mixed units on one panel cannot be converted automatically. Legacy weather screensaver.entity Explicit screensaver entities Current weather plus four daily entries; review forecast indices and overrides. screensaver.alternativeLayout screensaver.type: screensaver2 Review layout on your display.

items.title: Settings needing manual review
items.text:
Daily brightness schedules using time/value entries are supported, alongside static values and entity IDs. Use quoted HH:MM or HH:MM:SS times; sunrise/sunset expressions are not supported. Unknown card types cannot be saved. Legacy Berry driver update options, conditional entity fields (state, state_not, state_template), action_name, and service.* entries are retained and flagged where recognized, but are not implemented by this backend. Review weather overrides and unit fields against the screensaver reference.

Preserved fields are not a promise of feature parity. See the current cards, entities, and navigation references before migrating advanced setups. Legacy notification and physical-button examples are not migration instructions for this backend.

items.title: Connections, includes, and secrets
items.text:
AppDaemon MQTT/HASS plugin credentials are not imported from appdaemon.yaml. In normal add-on operation, Supervisor supplies the HA connection and discovered MQTT settings. For an external broker or standalone process, set the connection fields explicitly.

Inline !include and !secret values before uploading: the importer never reads files referenced by custom YAML tags. Duplicate keys, recursive aliases, and oversized input are rejected. Imports are limited to 1 MiB. Exported YAML contains any credentials explicitly stored in the configuration.

From add-on 4.8.1, updateMode and model-specific displayURL-* settings are supported for TFT updates and preserved on import. Review imported auto mode: it authorizes flashing without a confirmation when the installed TFT is older. berryURL remains unsupported.

items.title: Screensaver
items.text: screensaver is a required object in each panel config.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
key required type default description type no string screensaver Layout type (screensaver / screensaver2). entities no list none Screensaver entities. entity no string none Single-entity shortcut. statusIcon1 no object none Left status icon near date. statusIcon2 no object none Right status icon near date. doubleTapToUnlock no bool false Requires double tap when leaving screensaver. sleepTimeout no int panel sleepTimeout Per-screensaver timeout override.

Use entities to display weather and other Home Assistant data. An empty screensaver object is accepted when no entity content is wanted.

items.title: Screensaver entities
items.text:
Screensaver entities use the same entity format as other cards.

For weather.<entity> you can also use:

  • attribute (default temperature)
  • day (daily forecast index)
  • hour (hourly forecast index)
  • unit (suffix, default °C for temperature-like attributes)

items.title: Example
items.text:
screensaver:
  type: screensaver
  doubleTapToUnlock: true
  sleepTimeout: 30
  statusIcon1:
    entity: binary_sensor.front_door
    icon:
      "on": mdi:door-open
      "off": mdi:door-closed
    font: medium-icon
  statusIcon2:
    entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    icon: mdi:thermometer
  entities:
    - entity: weather.home
      attribute: temperature
    - entity: weather.home
      day: 1
      attribute: temperature
    - entity: weather.home
      day: 2
      attribute: temperature
    - entity: sensor.indoor_temperature
      icon: mdi:home-thermometer

items.title: Editor does not open
items.text: Check that the add-on is running and that its installed version includes the editor. Open it through Open Web UI or the sidebar. Direct access to port 8099 is rejected unless standalone editor mode is enabled. In standalone mode, set WEB_STANDALONE=true and a non-empty WEB_PASSWORD, publish port 8099, and log in with WEB_USERNAME (default admin) and that password. Inspect the add-on log for editor startup errors. The editor runs separately and can remain available while the backend waits for Home Assistant or MQTT.

items.title: Waiting for content
items.text:
1. Check the NSPanel Lovelace UI add-on log and MQTT broker log for connection or authentication errors.
  2. Verify the panel is connected to the same broker as the add-on.
  3. Match panelRecvTopic and panelSendTopic to Tasmota's topic and Full Topic settings; see MQTT configuration.
  4. Confirm the display firmware matches model and the Berry driver is installed.
  5. Stop any old add-on or AppDaemon instance controlling the same topics.

For ESPHome event mode, check use_ha_api: true, the event device ID, and the expected service in connection modes.

items.title: Changes do not appear
items.text:
Form and YAML edits are drafts until Save & apply. Advanced JSON fields have their own Apply advanced options to draft button. Inspect the log after saving: accepted YAML does not guarantee entity availability or panel connectivity.

The running add-on reads /config/panels.yaml inside its own container. This is not Home Assistant's configuration.yaml or AppDaemon's apps.yaml. A test-branch installation has separate configuration from the regular add-on. Check that you edited the installation actually driving your panel.

items.title: Import or save errors
items.text:
• Preview imports first. Unsupported card types and invalid brightness schedule entries must be corrected before saving.
  • Inline !include and !secret references. Uploaded YAML cannot read local files.
  • Provide unique receive topics, required date/locale fields, a screensaver object, and at least one card per panel.
  • If the configuration changed on disk, export your draft before Reload, then reapply your edits to the latest revision.
  • On a save failure, inspect the log and verify that the add-on can write its configuration directory.

items.title: Wrong page after leaving the screensaver
items.text: Use defaultCard: navigate.home at panel level, with a matching card key: home. See navigation. The AppDaemon location under screensaver is not used by this backend.

items.title: Restore a configuration
items.text: Each successful save backs up the previous file to /config/panels.yaml.bak. Export a known-good configuration before testing; this backup holds only the previous save. Restore by importing your exported YAML, or by copying the backup over panels.yaml in the add-on's configuration directory and restarting the add-on.

items.title: Information to include in a GitHub issue
items.text: Include the add-on version, panel model, connection mode, relevant panels.yaml section, and add-on log after startup/save. Remove passwords and tokens, including those in YAML exports. For AppDaemon installations, use legacy troubleshooting.
